name: promoter-specific chromatin binding
description: "Binding to a section of chromatin that is associated with gene promoter sequences of DNA." [PMID:19948729]

name: integrated stress response signaling
description: "The series of molecular signals generated in response to diverse stress stimuli required to restore cellular homeostasis. The core event in this pathway is the phosphorylation of eIF2 alpha by one of four members of the eIF2a kinase family (EIF2AK1/HRI, EIF2AK2/PKR, EIF2AK3/PERK and EIF2AK4/GCN2), which leads to a decrease in global protein synthesis and the induction of selected genes, including the transcription factor ATF4, that together promote cellular recovery." [PMID:27629041]

name: catalase complex
description: "A protein-containing complex that is capable of catalase activity." [GOC:bhm, PMID:10656833]

name: positive regulation of miRNA transcription
description: "Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of microRNA (miRNA) gene transcription." [GO_REF:0000058, GOC:dph, GOC:kmv, GOC:TermGenie, PMID:24699545]

name: positive regulation of miRNA metabolic process

name: response to activity
description: "Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an activity stimulus." [GOC:mtg_muscle]

name: regulation of miRNA transcription
description: "Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of microRNA (miRNA) gene transcription." [GO_REF:0000058, GOC:dph, GOC:kmv, GOC:TermGenie, PMID:24699545]

name: miRNA transcription
description: "The cellular synthesis of microRNA (miRNA) transcripts. MicroRNA genes are synthesized as primary (pri) miRNA transcripts and subsequently processed to produce the ~22nt miRNAs that function in gene regulation." [GOC:dph, GOC:kmv, PMID:18778799]

name: Reduced circulating catalase activity
description: Activity or concentration of catalase in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
